rubric: debounce(300) is applied to the query flow
flatMapLatest (or transformLatest/mapLatest) cancels the previous search when a new query arrives
A blank query short-circuits to an empty list without hitting the repository
Failures are caught inside the pipeline so the StateFlow keeps collecting
The flow is converted with stateIn(viewModelScope, ...) rather than collected into a var
notes:
The canonical Android interview pipeline. Every operator in it is there for a reason, and the interviewer will ask you which.

Traps:

- **`map` instead of `flatMapLatest`.** `map` waits for the slow request to finish before starting the next one, so results arrive out of order and the last one wins by luck. `flatMapLatest` cancels the previous `search` — that is the whole reason this is a Flow and not a callback.
- **`catch` outside the inner flow.** `catch` on the outer chain terminates the whole pipeline after the first failure: one network error and the screen is dead until the ViewModel is recreated. Keep it around the call that can fail.
- **`debounce` after `flatMapLatest`.** Then you have already fired the request you were trying to avoid.
- **`SharingStarted.Eagerly`** keeps the upstream alive while the app is backgrounded; `WhileSubscribed(5_000)` is the idiom because it survives a configuration change but not a real unsubscribe.
- A loading state is the natural follow-up — wrap the emissions in a sealed `UiState` and `onStart { emit(Loading) }` inside the `flatMapLatest` block.
